newsitem.title: UK: UK pop star ousted after drug endorsement.
newsitem.headline: UK pop star ousted after drug endorsement.

text.p: The lead singer of one of Britain's most popular rock groups was ousted by his fellow band members on Friday for endorsing the illegal drug Ecstacy.
Brian Harvey of "East 17" had said the mind-altering drug -- linked to a series of deaths at night clubs and parties across Britain -- was safe and brought out people's good side.
He was later forced to apologise for his remarks, which drew intense criticism from politicians and the public.
But the apology was not enough for his chart-topping London band, which said 22-year-old Harvey had been removed from the line-up "due to reasons of unacceptable behaviour.

"His recent remarks about drugs to the media have forced the other three members to demand that Brian leaves the band. The remaining three members of East 17 under no circumstances can condone the taking of Ecstacy or any other illegal substances," the group said in a statement.
Ecstasy, which is commonly known on the club scene as "E", is a favourite with many young people.
